summary: Macro backdrop for ags: headwind (score -7 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates 0; dollar −; brl −; mxn −; risk −; energy −; china −; breadth −. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Cotton +8.4%; weakest: Orange juice -14.5%.

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 4.94% (-11 bp in a month), 2-year 4.69% (+2 bp); 2s10s curve +25 bp (-13 bp in a month). Yields are little changed on the month. T-bill yield 4.15% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 104.04 (+1.8% in a month, +5.9% YTD). A stronger dollar makes US grain, oilseeds, cotton and meat dearer abroad. USD/BRL 5.514 (+3.1% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.654 (-0.2%); USD/MXN 19.67 (+5.2%); a sharply weaker peso cuts Mexico's buying power for US corn, pork, dairy and wheat (Mexico is the top buyer of all four).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -5.8% in a month (+6.6% YTD); VIX 23.8. Risk-off: funds tend to cut commodity length along with equities.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 83.08 $/bbl (-17.7% in a month), Brent 90.84, ULSD 3.675 $/gal (-19.6%), natural gas 3.49 (+0.6%). Lower crude weighs on soybean oil and corn through biofuel margins and on cotton via cheaper polyester.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -17.4% in a month, Shanghai Composite -2.0%, Hang Seng -1.7%, yuan +0.2% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 11 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (33%); S&P GSCI -13.1% in a month; gold -10.2%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
